title: Tor amplitude under comparison for Noetherian coefficients
statement:
Let $X$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated, $\Lambda$ a discrete Noetherian
ring and $K\in D^b_c(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$. For integers $a\leq b$, $K$ has Tor
amplitude in $[a,b]$ (that is, $K\otimes^{\mathrm L}_\Lambda N$ has cohomology
only in degrees $[a,b]$ for every $\Lambda$-module sheaf $N$ on $X_{\Et}$) if and
only if $\nu_X^*K$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ on $X_{\Proet}$. Consequently
$\nu_X^*$ restricts to an equivalence
$D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X_{\Et},\Lambda)\simeq\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$.

source.place: Tag 05VD, lemma-pullback-flat; blueprint paragraph Flatness is preserved

proof.text:
Exactness of $F$ implies $H^q(FC)=F(H^qC)$: apply $F$ to the kernel of $d^q$, the image of $d^{q-1}$, and their quotient. Consequently termwise $F$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms and induces the comparison on derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Its total left derived functor equals this termwise functor, since the image of a resolving quasi-isomorphism is already a quasi-isomorphism. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] to the ringed morphism of step 1 and to $K,N[0]$. We obtain
$$F(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N)\simeq FK\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}FN.$$
Here $FN$ is still a sheaf in degree zero. Also $FM=0$ implies $M=0$ for a module sheaf: faithfulness sends equality $F(1_M)=F(0)$ back to $1_M=0$. We will use this to reflect vanishing of cohomology, not to assert that every pro-etale module is classical.

source.place: Tag 07A4, lemma-pullback-tensor-product; blueprint paragraph Tor amplitude is detected

proof.text: Suppose first that $K$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$. Testing against $R$ gives $H^qK=0$ outside $[a,b]$: ordinary tensor with $R$ is the identity, so the same is true of its K-flat derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor]. By [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category] choose a representative $C$ with $C^q=0$ for $q>b$. Apply [lem-pc-kflat-bounded-flat-replacement] on $(X_{\Et},R)$, with upper bound $b$, to obtain a quasi-isomorphism $P\to C$, all $P^q$ flat and $P^q=0$ for $q>b$. The complex $P$ is K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site]. Therefore [def-kun-derived-tensor] computes $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N$ by $P\otimes_R N$ for every etale module sheaf $N$. In particular $H^{a-1}(P\otimes_R N)=0$ for every $N$.

source.place: Tag 08G1, lemma-tor-amplitude, proof, bounded-above flat model; Tag 06YQ, lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat; blueprint paragraph Tor amplitude is preserved

proof.text:
Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-flat-opcycles-tor-criterion] to $P$ and $n=a$. Since $N$ is placed in degree zero, the maps $x\otimes y\mapsto y\otimes x$ identify $P^q\otimes_R N$ with $N\otimes_R P^q$ in every degree and commute with the differentials: the tensor symmetry sign is $(-1)^{q\cdot0}=1$. Thus its hypothesis is exactly the universal ordinary-tensor exactness in degree $a-1$ established in step 3. Thus $Q=\operatorname{coker}(P^{a-1}\to P^a)$ is flat. Form the good truncation
$$S_K=\tau_{\ge a}P=[Q\longrightarrow P^{a+1}\longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow P^b]$$
as in [def-kun-truncations]. Its first differential is induced by $d^a$, which kills the image of $d^{a-1}$. This truncation retains $H^q(P)$ for $q\ge a$ and has zero cohomology below $a$; since $H^q(P)=H^q(K)=0$ for $q<a$, the natural map $P\to S_K$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Hence $S_K$ represents $K$, consists of flat sheaves, and is zero outside $[a,b]$. This writes out the shortening argument instead of citing the finite-ring comparison lemma as a general theorem.

source.place: Tag 08G0, lemma-last-one-flat, and Tag 08G1, lemma-tor-amplitude, last paragraph of proof; blueprint paragraph Tor amplitude is preserved

proof.text: Apply $F$ termwise to $S_K$. Step 1 makes every term flat, and exactness makes $F(S_K)$ a representative of $FK$. It vanishes outside $[a,b]$, so it is K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site]. For an arbitrary pro-etale $S$-module sheaf $M$, not assumed classical, [def-weil-derived-tensor] therefore computes $FK\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}M$ by $F(S_K)\otimes_S M$. Its degree-$q$ term is $F(S_K^q)\otimes_S M$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], which is zero for $q\notin[a,b]$. Its cohomology is zero there as well. This proves preservation with the same interval.

source.place: Tag 06YQ, lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat, and Tag 08G1, lemma-tor-amplitude, implication (2) to (1); blueprint paragraph Tor amplitude is preserved

proof.text:
Conversely suppose $FK$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$, and let $N$ be any etale $R$-module sheaf. The tensor-pullback isomorphism of step 2 identifies $F(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N)$ with $FK\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}FN$, whose cohomology vanishes outside $[a,b]$ by the hypothesis. Exactness gives
$$F\bigl(H^q(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N)\bigr)\simeq H^q\bigl(FK\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}FN\bigr)=0\qquad(q\notin[a,b]).$$
Faithfulness of $F$ then gives $H^q(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N)=0$ as proved in step 2. Since $N$ was arbitrary, $K$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$. Neither invertibility of a coefficient exponent nor finiteness of the coefficient set is needed.

By [sk-thm-pe-constructible-comparison], under the given qcqs and discrete Noetherian hypotheses $F$ is an equivalence $D^b_c(X_{\Et},\Lambda)\to\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$. Both finite-Tor categories are the full subcategories selected by existence of a single finite interval with the stated universal tensor vanishing; on the pro-etale side this is [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude]. Steps 5 and 6 identify these object predicates. The restricted functor is fully faithful because the ambient functor is. For any object $L$ of $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ choose $K$ and an ambient isomorphism $FK\simeq L$ using essential surjectivity. An interval for $L$ is an interval for $FK$, so step 6 puts $K$ in $D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$. Thus the restricted functor is essentially surjective and gives the claimed equivalence.
